title: What Is The Cost In PostgreSQL EXPLAIN Query
snippet: Execution cost is the planner's guess at how long it takes to run the statement, measured in relative cost units. The execution cost has two options: start-up and total, where the start-up cost shows how long it takes before the first row can be processed, while the total cost shows how long it takes to process all the rows.
claim: Cost tables separate startup cost from total cost, enabling planners to predict both latency-to-first-result and total execution duration.
